jobs.description: Clinical Instructor of Dental Hygiene Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Please see Special Instructions for more details. Applicants should submit:Cover letterCurriculum vitae or resumeContact information for three professional referencesCopies of professional licenses and certifications (upon request)The University of South Dakota is committed to creating a welcoming learning and working environment that supports excellence, collaboration, and service to the people of South Dakota. Posting Details Posting Details Logo Institution The University of South Dakota Working Title Clinical Instructor of Dental Hygiene Posting Number F01915P Department USD-Dental Hygiene Physical Location of Position (City) Sioux Falls Posting Text The University of South Dakota Department of Dental Hygiene invites applications for a full-time (12-month, 100%) Clinical Faculty position based in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. This position is part of an innovative partnership between the University of South Dakota and Falls Community Health Dental Clinic that combines academic instruction, clinical supervision, and direct patient care in a community health setting. The successful candidate will supervise dental hygiene students during clinical education experiences, and deliver direct patient care during designated clinic sessions. This faculty member will play an integral role in preparing future dental hygienists while advancing access to quality oral healthcare throughout the region. Essential Responsibilities Teaching & Clinical Education Supervise dental hygiene students in the clinical setting while ensuring patient safety and high-quality care. Provide instruction, mentoring, and evaluation of student clinical performance. Facilitate student competency assessments and clinical skill development. Participate in faculty calibration, curriculum development, program assessment, and accreditation activities. Ensure compliance with Commission on Dental Accreditation (CODA) standards, South Dakota Board of Dentistry regulations, and University policies. Collaborate with Falls Community Health Dental Clinic staff to coordinate student schedules and clinical learning experiences. Clinical Practice Provide direct preventive dental hygiene services within the scope of South Dakota licensure during designated clinical practice periods. Maintain accurate clinical documentation utilizing the clinic’s electronic health record. Collaborate with dentists, dental hygienists, and other healthcare professionals to provide comprehensive patient care. Support quality improvement, infection prevention, and patient-centered care initiatives. Faculty Service & Professional Engagement Participate in department, university, and community service activities. Maintain professional licensure, certifications, and clinical competency. Engage in professional development appropriate to faculty rank. Demonstrate a commitment to community engagement and service. Required Qualifications Graduate of a Commission on Dental Accreditation (CODA) accredited Dental Hygiene program. Bachelor of Science in Dental Hygiene (BSDH). Current South Dakota dental hygiene license or eligibility for South Dakota licensure. South Dakota certification to administer local anesthesia and nitrous oxide/oxygen sedation, or eligibility to obtain certification. Current Healthcare Provider CPR certification. In good standing with the South Dakota Board of Dentistry. Demonstrated commitment to community engagement and service. Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills. Ability to work collaboratively with students, faculty, healthcare providers, and community partners. Preferred Qualifications Master of Science in Dental Hygiene (MSDH) or a closely related field, or current enrollment in a graduate degree program. Three or more years of clinical dental hygiene experience. Previous preclinical and/or clinical teaching experience in a CODA-accredited dental hygiene program. Experience working in community or public health settings. Knowledge of CODA accreditation standards and outcomes assessment. Work ScheduleThis is a full-time, 12-month faculty position. Clinical education activities are generally scheduled Tuesday through Thursday during the academic year. The faculty member will also provide direct patient care at Falls Community Health Dental Clinic during designated clinic sessions, anticipated to average approximately one and one-half days per week (Mondays, Fridays). This position offers a unique opportunity to combine teaching, clinical practice, and community service through a partnership between the University of South Dakota and Falls Community Health Dental Clinic. Faculty maintain an active clinical role while educating future dental hygienists, expanding access to care, and strengthening South Dakota’s oral health workforce. The University of South Dakota is committed to fostering an environment of academic excellence, collaboration, innovation, and service.Candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. Sponsorship is not available for this position. jobs.title: Department Head for Mathematics and Statistics and Professor
jobs.description: Department Head for Mathematics and Statistics and Professor Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Posting Details Posting Details Logo Institution South Dakota State University Working Title Department Head for Mathematics and Statistics and Professor Posting Number F01929P Department SDSU-Mathematics & Statistics Physical Location of Position (City) Brookings Posting Text The Department of Mathematics and Statistics (Math & Stat) at South Dakota State University (SDSU) invites applicants for the Department Head and Professor position. We are looking for a dynamic and collaborative leader who is committed to providing a rigorous and practical educational experience with an emphasis on expanding federally funded research and graduate programs to support South Dakota State University’s R1 Our Way mission, as well as establishing and providing scientific support to local industry and government. This position is 12-month, full-time, benefits-eligible position, located in Brookings SD and reports to the Dean of the Jerome J. Johr College of Engineering (JJLCOE). Anticipated start of January 2027. The Department of Mathematics and Statistics offers the following undergraduate programs: AS in Data Science, BS in Data Science, and BS in Mathematics. The BS in Mathematics includes the following specialty areas: Actuarial/Financial Concentration, Applied Mathematics Concentration, Data Science Concentration, and Teaching Specialization. Graduate programs include the following: Data Science Certificate, MS in Data Science, MS in Mathematics, MS in Statistics, and PhD in Computational Science and Statistics. Many students in our vibrant graduate program serve in GTA and GRA positions. Currently, the department has approximately 180 undergraduate majors, 60 graduate students, 17 tenure-track faculty, and 9 full-time lecturers. Must be authorized to work in the U.S. Sponsorship is not available for this position.KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:The Department Head will work closely with the Dean and the leadership team of the JJLCOE to promote the land-grant mission and an ambitious agenda to address the world’s grand challenges in the areas of mathematics, statistics, and data science. The selected candidate is expected to be the leader in identifying future areas of growth and investment while providing organizational and administrative expertise to the Department and the College. The candidate is expected to steer the growth of the department consistent with SDSU’s refreshed strategic plan titled “Pathway to Premier 2030”. The strategic plan includes a goal to elevate SDSU as a research university and pursue a pathway to achieve designation as an R1 Research University by Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. It is imperative that this position maintains an understanding of current and emerging needs in mathematics, statistics, and data science to guide both research and teaching initiatives. It is the Department Head’s responsibility to lead the faculty in their efforts to provide high-quality service courses at all levels, engage with client departments to determine their course needs, monitor trends in general education and service courses, and implement high-impact teaching and learning strategies. Along with leadership, the Department Head is an advocate for the Department of Mathematics and Statistics both within and outside the University, fostering a commitment to interdisciplinary and interagency collaborationBENEFITS: SDState offers a wide range of excellent benefits including medical, dental, and flexible benefits, retirement plans, compensation packages, paid holidays, and vacation leave. We offer a generous retirement plan that includes 6% matching, 10 hours of annual leave each month, 9.34 hours of sick leave each month, and eleven paid holidays. Employees also have access to internal and state-sponsored training as well as reduced tuition for state-supported courses at all State of South Dakota academic institutions. Relocation benefits are available per university’s guidelines. QUALIFICATIONSMINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Ph.D. in mathematics, statistics, data science, or closely related field by date of application. A distinguished record of teaching, research, scholarship, and service consistent with eligibility for tenure and rank of Professor at SDSU in the Math & Stat Department. Standards documents are available upon request. Evidence of effective leadership and administrative skills including management of academic and research programs, managing complex budgets, fiscal matters, and/or personnel within an academic setting. Experience securing competitive grants for research from federal, industry, and/or corporate sources. An understanding of the land-grant mission. Effective written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Experience mentoring faculty in developing strategies for pursuing external funding and in creating strong research programs. Experience in academic administration, including the development, evaluation and oversight of undergraduate academic programs, curricula and/or instructional operations. Experience interacting and cultivating relationships with businesses in the medical, insurance, and financial sectors in the region. Familiarity with ABET accreditation process. Engagement in professional organizations for mathematics & statistics (e.g., SIAM, AMS, MAA, ASA, etc.) APPLICATION PROCESS:SDState accepts applications through an on-line employment site. To apply, visit: https://yourfuture.sdbor.edu, search by the position title, view the job announcement, and click on “apply for this job.” This system will guide you through the electronic application form. jobs.title: Klingbeil Endowed Department Head and Professor
Selma Kendrick Assistant, Associate, or Full Professorship in Nursing
jobs.description: Selma Kendrick Assistant, Associate, or Full Professorship in Nursing Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Posting Details Posting Details Logo Institution South Dakota State University Working Title Selma Kendrick Assistant, Associate, or Full Professorship in Nursing Posting Number F01880P Department SDSU-Graduate Nursing Physical Location of Position (City) Rapid City Posting Text The endowment holder for the Selma Kendrick Endowed Professorship in Nursing in the SDState College of Nursing will partner with the college’s Native American Nursing Education Center with the goal of growing research and scholarly activities to impact the health of Native American Communities in South Dakota. The College of Nursing prides itself in commitment to excellence in education, research, and clinical practice. The College of Nursing is especially interested in candidates who have significant potential to build extramural funding to support the goals of improving health in Native American communities. This position is located in Rapid City, South Dakota. This position is a 12-month, full-time, benefits-eligible position. The SDSU College of Nursing, located in Brookings, Rapid City, and Sioux Falls, has a long history of exceptional nursing education and this is recognized through its designation as a Center of Excellence in Nursing Education by the National League for Nursing. The college’s fully accredited Healthcare Simulation Center encompassing all three sites is further evidence of our commitment to high quality education for all students. SDSU Nursing’s history of excellence, innovation and achievement across its graduate and undergraduate programs provides an excellent foundation for growth and innovation. Must be authorized to work in the U.S. Sponsorship is not available for this position.KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Embedded in the SDSU College of Nursing’s Native American Nursing Education Center (NANEC), this endowed professorship will fulfill a collaborative role with the advising and mentoring team in NANEC to: Build supportive relationships with Native American Students across the college. Develop collaborative relationships with tribal communities across South Dakota. Develop teams responsible for innovative health research that impacts the health and well-being of indigenous populations across South Dakota. Grow a body of health research that informs health policy, population well-being, and healthy communities. Develop consistent extramural funding to support the research endeavors to support NANEC and the innovative research focus for Native American populations. Support teaching teams and NANEC in development of pedagogically sound educational offerings. BENEFITS: SDState offers a wide range of excellent benefits including medical, dental, and flexible benefits, retirement plans, compensation packages, paid holidays, and vacation leave. We offer a generous retirement plan that includes 6% matching, 10 hours of annual leave each month, 9.34 hours of sick leave each month, and eleven paid holidays. Employees also have access to internal and state-sponsored training as well as reduced tuition for state-supported courses at all State of South Dakota academic institutions. Relocation benefits are available per university’s guidelines. QUALIFICATIONS MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Bachelor’s Degree in Nursing, completed by application date; Graduate Degree in Nursing, completed by application date; A Ph.D. in nursing or related field, completed by start date; Teaching experience at the undergraduate or graduate levels; A history of successfully funded research and relevant clinical practice; Licensed by the South Dakota Board of Nursing or eligible for licensure as a registered nurse as evidenced by current licensure in another state; Hold a national and/or international reputation for scholarship in Indigenous and rural health, community engaged research, and interdisciplinary approaches that inform health policy, strengthen educational practices, and improve population health outcomes, and/or aligned areas of value that will advance the strengths of the college. Experience developing collaborative partnerships across academic, government, industry, and nonprofit sectors; Effective written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills; Valid driver’s license, or ability to obtain one within 30 days of hire, and willingness to travel. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Active program of research and dissemination, preferably related to Native American health and well-being; Experience with simulation technology and distance delivery; Demonstrated potential or ability to work collaboratively in interdisciplinary teams; Evidence of service to the nursing profession. APPLICATION PROCESS:This system will guide you through the electronic application form. This employment site will also require the attachment of a cover letter, which should specifically address how the candidate meets the qualifications as outlined in the advertisement, curriculum vitae, and a reference page with the contact information for three professional references. Email applications will not be accepted. Please contact SDState Human Resources at (605) 688-4128 if you require assistance with this process. Any offer of employment is contingent on the university’s verification of credentials and other information required by law and/or university policies, including but not limited to, successful completion of a criminal background check. SDState is a tobacco free environment. It is the policy of the University to maintain a drug-free environment and to thereby establish, promote, and maintain a safe and healthy working and learning environment for employees and students. This position is subject to South Dakota State University’s Drug and Alcohol Testing Policy 4:14.
